# MySQLd Receiver

Receives MySQL server metrics by running the Prometheus
[mysqld_exporter](https://github.com/prometheus/mysqld_exporter)
as an OpenTelemetry Collector receiver.

## Configuration

Configure the receiver in the Collector YAML. `exporter_config` contains the
upstream exporter's Go configuration, with field names written in snake_case.
For example, native password authentication uses:

```yaml
receivers:
  mysqld_exporter/local:
    exporter_config:
      data_source_name: "exporter:${env:MYSQL_PASSWORD}@tcp(localhost:3306)/"
```

Each receiver instance monitors one database endpoint. Add named receiver
instances to monitor additional endpoints, each with its own credentials or IAM
settings. This receiver does not load `.my.cnf` files or standalone exporter
`auth_module` sections.

### AWS IAM authentication

Set `exporter_config.auth_provider.type` to `aws-iam` to authenticate to Amazon
RDS or Aurora MySQL using IAM tokens:

```yaml
receivers:
  mysqld_exporter/rds:
    scrape_interval: 30s
    exporter_config:
      data_source_name: "exporter@tcp(mydb.123456789012.us-east-1.rds.amazonaws.com:3306)/?tls=true"
      auth_provider:
        type: aws-iam
        region: us-east-1
        # Optional: assume another IAM role using the discovered AWS credentials.
        # role_arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/Exporter

exporters:
  debug: {}

service:
  pipelines:
    metrics:
      receivers: [mysqld_exporter/rds]
      exporters: [debug]
```

| Setting | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | Yes, when `auth_provider` is set | Authentication provider. Currently only `aws-iam` is supported. |
| `region` | No | AWS Region of the database. If omitted, uses the AWS SDK's region configuration, including the environment, shared AWS config, or EC2 metadata. |
| `role_arn` | No | IAM role to assume before signing database authentication tokens. |

Omit `auth_provider` or set it to `null` for native MySQL authentication. An
explicit provider block must specify a supported `type`; unknown settings are
rejected.

IAM mode requires a database user, a TCP endpoint, and TLS without plaintext
fallback. Leave the DSN password empty. `tls=false`, `tls=preferred`, static
passwords, and Unix sockets are rejected during receiver creation. TLS is
enabled automatically if the DSN does not specify a TLS mode; `tls=true` makes
that explicit. The Collector host's trust store must trust the database's
server certificate. See the [RDS TLS documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/UsingWithRDS.SSL.html)
for its CA certificates. `tls=skip-verify` disables certificate verification.

Enable [IAM database authentication](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/UsingWithRDS.IAMDBAuth.html)
on the database and configure the database user for IAM authentication with the
usual [exporter grants](https://github.com/prometheus/mysqld_exporter#required-grants).
Use the actual RDS or Aurora endpoint in the DSN; tokens are signed for that
endpoint and database user. The signing identity needs
[`rds-db:connect`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/UsingWithRDS.IAMDBAuth.IAMPolicy.html)
permission for that database user. When `role_arn` is set, the caller must be
allowed to assume the role and trusted by it, and the assumed role needs the
database connection permission.

AWS credentials come from the [SDK's default credential chain](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-go/v2/developer-guide/configure-gosdk.html),
including environment credentials, shared AWS profiles, and workload IAM roles.
Use `AWS_PROFILE` to select a shared profile. Credentials are loaded when a
database connection is opened, so successful receiver creation does not verify
AWS permissions or database connectivity. The exporter generates an IAM token
for each new physical connection and retains the SDK credential cache for the
lifetime of that receiver instance.
